raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "absolute size of the cuboid",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 7 specifies 16×2×2 equal coarse cubes, fixing the aspect ratio, but never gives their side length. The final mesh counts are determined; the common geometric scale is not.",
      "readings": [
        "Coarse cube side 1: domain dimensions 16×2×2.",
        "Coarse cube side 1/16: domain dimensions 1×1/8×1/8."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "load centered on the right-hand face",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 7 says the load acts in the middle of the right-hand face and refers to Fig. 2(a). Neither the text nor its caption specifies whether this is a nodal force, line load, or loaded patch, or gives nodal weights. Write the domain dimensions as L×W×H.",
      "readings": [
        "A concentrated force at the existing central node (L,W/2,H/2).",
        "A uniform line load at x=L, z=H/2, spanning 0≤y≤W.",
        "A uniform traction on the centered patch x=L, 3W/8≤y≤5W/8, 3H/8≤z≤5H/8."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "sign of the z-directed load",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 7 specifies direction z without a sign; the arrow in Fig. 2(a) is unavailable. Reversing this sole load leaves compliance and the optimal density unchanged in the stated linear model.",
      "readings": [
        "Load in the +z direction.",
        "Load in the -z direction."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_magnitude",
      "entity": "total applied force",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "No numerical load magnitude or traction intensity is supplied for CANT-16-2-2-5. Table 1 objective values cannot identify it independently of the other missing scales.",
      "readings": [
        "Total resultant magnitude 1 in consistent force units.",
        "Total resultant magnitude 10 in the same force units."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "volume_fraction",
      "entity": "material budget V",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Eq. (1) defines sum(rho_i)=V, but Sec. 7.1 and Table 1 give neither V nor its fraction of the fully dense domain. For a uniform upper density rho_max, that fraction is V/(262144 rho_max).",
      "readings": [
        "Volume fraction 0.1.",
        "Volume fraction 0.25.",
        "Volume fraction 0.5."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "upper density bounds and density normalization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Eq. (1) permits an upper-bound vector, but no numerical upper bound is specified for this example. The method-specific lower bounds are explicitly given and are not ambiguous.",
      "readings": [
        "rho_max=1 in every element.",
        "rho_max=0.5 in every element, with the same numerical V."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "overall elastic stiffness scale",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The element stiffness matrices are introduced abstractly in Sec. 1; no Young's modulus or equivalent overall constitutive scale is given in Secs. 6.2 or 7.1.",
      "readings": [
        "Reference Young's modulus E=1.",
        "Reference Young's modulus E=2 in the same consistent units."
      ],
      "effect": "scale_only"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "dimensionless constitutive properties",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The text does not specify isotropy, Poisson's ratio, or an anisotropic constitutive tensor and its orientation. Single-material linear elasticity alone does not determine these.",
      "readings": [
        "Isotropic 3D elasticity with Poisson's ratio 0.25.",
        "Isotropic 3D elasticity with Poisson's ratio 0.30.",
        "Orthotropic elasticity aligned with x,y,z: Ex=2E0, Ey=Ez=E0, all three shear moduli 0.4E0, and nu_xy=nu_xz=nu_yz=0.25, with reciprocal ratios implied."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "numerical construction of the hexahedral element stiffness",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.2 specifies trilinear displacement and elementwise constant density, but does not specify quadrature or stabilization. The structured 256×32×32 element grid itself is uniquely determined.",
      "readings": [
        "Fully integrated trilinear bricks using 2×2×2 Gauss quadrature.",
        "One-point integrated trilinear bricks with hourglass stabilization."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial PBM penalty parameters",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3.2 gives the initial primal variables, multipliers, update factors, and penalty floors, but not the initial p_i, lower q_i, or upper q_i required by Algorithm 1.",
      "readings": [
        "Initialize all three penalty-parameter arrays to 1.",
        "Initialize all three arrays to 0.1.",
        "Initialize p_i=1 and both q_i arrays to 0.1."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "PBM Newton backtracking",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Algorithm 2, line 5 names an Armijo backtracking search but gives no sufficient-decrease constant, contraction factor, or initial trial step.",
      "readings": [
        "Initial step 1, Armijo constant 0.0001, contraction factor 0.5.",
        "Initial step 0.5, Armijo constant 0.01, contraction factor 0.8."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "multigrid Gauss-Seidel smoothing schedule",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6.1 names Gauss-Seidel smoothing but does not give sweep counts, sweep directions, scalar versus nodal-block updates, or ordering.",
      "readings": [
        "One scalar forward presweep and one backward postsweep with lexicographic ordering.",
        "Two scalar forward presweeps and two backward postsweeps with lexicographic ordering.",
        "One forward and one backward sweep using 3×3 displacement blocks at each node."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "multigrid coarsest-level solution",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 6.1–6.2 define the hierarchy and Galerkin coarse operators but do not specify how the coarsest system is solved.",
      "readings": [
        "An exact coarse solve using Cholesky factorization.",
        "An approximate coarse solve using ten symmetric Gauss-Seidel sweeps."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "MINRES initial guesses",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 6 supplies stopping tolerances but does not state the initial guess for successive equilibrium or reduced Newton solves. This matters for reproducing the inexact solves and Table 1 iteration counts.",
      "readings": [
        "Start every linear solve from zero.",
        "Reuse the previous solution of the corresponding linear system as a warm start."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial DOC density field",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Initial densities are specified for PBM and IP in Secs. 3.2 and 4.1, but not for DOC in Sec. 5 or the example discussion.",
      "readings": [
        "Uniform initial density rho_i=V/m.",
        "Initially fully dense: rho_i=rho_max everywhere."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial shifted IP barrier values",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 initializes r=s=0.01, but Algorithm 3 assigns r=r_plus and s=s_plus on its first pass before line 11 has computed those stored values.",
      "readings": [
        "Initialize r_plus=s_plus=0.01 as well.",
        "Initialize r_plus and s_plus from the initial complementarity measures using sigma_r=sigma_s=0.2."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "PBM lower-bound multiplier update",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 3.2 defines the lower-bound penalty argument as -lower_nu_i/lower_q_i. The generic update (11) therefore uses that negative argument, but Algorithm 1, line 7 prints a positive argument for updating lower_mu_i.",
      "readings": [
        "Update lower_mu_i using phi_prime(-lower_nu_i/lower_q_i), consistently with the defined penalty.",
        "Use the printed Algorithm 1 update with phi_prime(+lower_nu_i/lower_q_i)."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "PBM reduced Newton right-hand side and multiplier recovery",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "For this example's PBM lower density bound of zero, Eq. (17) gives the lower-nu residual as rho_prime-lower_mu_prime. The corresponding block printed below Eq. (20) and in Eq. (21) instead contains rho_prime+lower_mu_prime.",
      "readings": [
        "Build the reduced right-hand side and recovery from the gradient of Eq. (16), using the negative lower_mu_prime term.",
        "Use the positive lower_mu_prime term printed with Eqs. (20)–(21)."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "IP Newton residual and reduced updates",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "In Sec. 4.1, the printed residual places upper-nu terms with signs and blocks inconsistent with the KKT equations and Jacobian (23). The reduced formulas also disagree with Newton elimination; for example, Eq. (27) uses rho where elimination requires Delta_rho.",
      "readings": [
        "Construct the residual from the stated KKT conditions and derive all Newton increments consistently from Jacobian (23).",
        "Implement the printed residual and reduced formulas (25)–(28) literally."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "IP volume-multiplier sign in the duality-gap test",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "The dual formulation (2) uses a -alpha term in the element constraint, whereas Sec. 4.1 stationarity uses +alpha. Sec. 4 nevertheless says alpha has the same meaning and Algorithm 3 evaluates the duality gap using Eq. (7).",
      "readings": [
        "Keep the printed IP stationarity convention and pass -alpha_IP to the duality-gap formula.",
        "Use the dual alpha convention throughout and consistently change the IP stationarity and Newton formulas."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    }
  ]
}
